lines.english: ("Like I said, she's currently not accepting any direct interviews… Yes, I apologize. That is what she wishes.")
("Yes, yes, an interview by email would be acceptable. I know it will cause a lot of hassle, but I hope you understand.")
("I understand. We'll make sure it's settled by the 14th. Auf Wiedersehen.")
"Haah…"
As I cut the call, I see the time is 01:15 on the LCD.
The conversation was with a newspaper company we've known for a long time, but it seems that their management has changed, so I had to spend the whole day explaining things.
…Having such a long phone call in the middle of the night and not losing my cool is only because I understood the position of the other person.
"Sorry, did I wake you?"
The reason I managed to hold in my anger was because I had been in the shoes of the other person.
"No, I just woke up on my own."
I look behind me on the bed, and see a girl with long black hair looking at me.
…No point in beating around the bush, that girl is Kazusa.
"But it must've been annoying. Perhaps I really should relocate my office to…"
"You can't. I won't allow it."
"Most people would say the opposite…"
"The sound of your keyboard, the sound of your email notification, and the businesslike voice you have when you're on the phone are like a lullaby for me."
"That makes no sense…"
"Just shut up and continue working here, and that'll do… Here we go…!"
"…You're heavy!"
"You should be happy to have something to rest your back on. Your sitting posture is awful."
She crawls out of bed, and for some reason, sits down on the floor with her back turned against mine.
Her weight leans on my back. She relaxes her muscles as if leaving her whole body in my care.
…Not that I don't get the reason. She just wants to snuggle up to me.

Even when I'm working, I'll find her sleeping on my lap before I know it. Sometimes she falls asleep with her head on my shoulder, and other times she falls asleep with her back against mine like she's doing right now. I think she's mistaking me for a pillow.
How should I put this… I never expected her to be this clingy.
"By the way, about this phone call… they were asking questions about your next performance in Prague…"
"Oh, you can just answer whatever you want."
"…Again?"
Maybe it's because she likes using me as a pillow so much that she allowed me to move my workplace home.
But she completely opposes the idea of creating a room meant for working at home, so in the end, I'm left doing my job here in the bedroom.
"But if I give some half-assed answer to them, you'll have to fix everything. So me talking to them is completely pointless."
"You're absolutely right. The reason it all comes to nothing is because your answers are always half-assed."
Kazusa understands. She knows I spend almost all day working.
Because the pianist in the center of it all can do nothing else but play the piano.
Sometimes she even makes her manager put on her underwear for her… Not that I don't do that in my free time anyway.
"What's the problem…? You were the one who said I only have to play the piano… I'm just being the woman you wanted me to be."
"Well, I suppose that's fine."
"…Seriously, for how long do you plan on spoiling me?"
"Do you dislike it?"
"Don't ask questions you know the answer to. You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world."
Ever since then, Kazusa has continued playing the piano.
And I've become responsible for the lifeline of Touma Youko Office PLC, as Kazusa's manager.
Since then, the only people the European branch consists of is the pianist herself, and her sole manager, just like in Japan.
By the way, that sole pianist with the household name "Touma Kazusa" attempted to replace it with her new real name.
But due to the strategic weight behind the "Touma" name, her European branch manager rejected her proposal, which led to lots of grumbling on her part.
"If you're going to sleep, then return to bed. You have a concert next month, and I won't tolerate you catching a cold."
"Then you can just come do your job in bed. Don't make it my fault."
"If I do that, you'll just be up to more mischief. I won't be able to do my job at all."
"Of course you won't. You think I can just lie there and hold back as we're in bed together?"
"Ah, you're making no sense…"
Anyway, aside from that…
This is our way of being able to be with each other more during our busy schedules. We've already firmly gotten used to this mingling of our work and private lives.
Now the only times we're not together is when Kazusa is spending her ten hours a day playing the piano.
…To Kazusa, that was her limit.
"Oh, it's from mo… I mean, from the President."
"…Is she doing well?"
But I, too, never thought about separating from Kazusa, not even once.
As much as our feelings for each other are an obvious reason, there are some circumstances that prevent me from leaving her alone. And there are circumstances that prevent me from being alone…
"Yeah, she seems to be doing just fine. She says she attended a lecture in Hokkaido just last month… One about sea urchins, salmon roe, crabs and scallops apparently."
"Tell her to get back to her hospital bed… if she's doing that well, she should just come to Vienna."
Two years have passed since then.
Kazusa is still playing the piano. I am working hard at my new job.
…We are living our lives the best we can.
Yet even then, sometimes I wake up to hear Kazusa crying in her sleep.
And sometimes, I wake up to see Kazusa looking at me with a worried expression.
The two of us never talk about it. Instead, we reach out our fingers and wipe off each other's tears, and heal our invisible wounds.
That's why Kazusa never leaves my side. That's why I'm still always right next to her.
…It's been two years.
We still refuse to talk about that country.
Not about the place we spent so much of our lives in. Not about the profound memories we share. Not about the people we treasured…
It's because we think of it so much that we never talk about it, always averting our eyes and covering our ears as we live our daily lives.
To the point where we can't forget about it even for a moment…
"And now, we'll proceed to the weather forecast. Yanagihara-san."
"Thank you and good evening, I'm Yanagihara Tomo. I'll be reporting on the weather this evening from the roof of the East Asia TV building like always!"
"Yanagihara-san, looks like the wind is pretty strong over there!"
"It really is! Just take a look at the temperature. It's 6:40 PM right now, and it's pointing to 2°C."
"Regarding the Kanto region this evening, we can expect some intense cold due to low atmospheric pressure in the west."
"What the hell is this article? 'Weather announcer Yanagihara in passionate love affair with first place baseball rookie?' Both the title and the contents are just awful."
"Ah, I had a feeling you'd say that. I guess I got a bit carried away with the vulgarity."
"That's not what I said at all. I'm saying you haven't gone far enough!"
"Y-You think so?"

"You don't have any pictures of the crime. Your only comments come from official responses… How much research did you actually do on this? Have you ever heard of surprise interviews early in the morning or late at night?"
"Vulgar material deserves to be in vulgar articles. If you want to write some high-class thesis, then do it once you've gotten at least one scoop."
"But I asked myself when I was researching this article… that maybe this kind of article doesn't suit our Kaiou Graph."
"If it doesn't suit us, then just submit it to the editing department next door. You're much more an employee of Kaiousha than a member of Kaiou Graph."
"But I'm new here. I don't have those kinds of connections."
"Then ask your superiors for help! I'll help, so will Kizaki-san. Our managing editor, Hamada, is always available… even Suzuki-san would help."
"Hey, why am I below you in the list?"
"You think you can get away with keeping the mindset of a salaryman here? Don't underestimate this business."
"You thought it was going to be an easy job at first too…"
"Stay out of it, outsiders! Did I say anything wrong?"
"No… you're completely right, but…"
"I was just so moved. To think our little Macchan has grown so much."
"I have responsibilities too, you know. Not just for myself, but also to educate the new guys. We have the responsibility now to maintain the company."
"Matsuoka…"
"Well said, Matsuoka. You're completely right!"
"Right you are, Managing Editor!"
"But that article was supposed to be your job! You didn't want to do it so you tossed it to someone else, didn't you!?"
"Like I said, it's all part of their education!"
"He's really grown so much. Just perfect at his job."
"S-Sorry to keep you waiting!"
"You sure did! I've been stuck shivering in this cold forever!"
"Sorry, sorry. Cleaning the seminar room took longer than I thought."
"Just look at how cold my hands are! I can barely feel them anymore."
"Ah, you're right…"
"Yeah…"
"…Can you still not feel them?"
"…Let's go."
"It's about time for graduation."
"It is…"
"Four years passed just like that…"
"Still, so much happened. So many things."
"Yeah…"
"U-Um, anyway… where do you want to go today?"
"Ah…"
"Do you want to eat out somewhere? Or if you're okay with waiting, perhaps I can make something for you?"
"Actually, while we're at it, do you want to spend the evening in my room? Perhaps we could buy some wine. You can stay, right?"
"Ah, aah… well…"
"Alright, it's decided! Then let's go to the supermarket by the station…"
"Sorry! Today I really have to be at home!"
"Huh, huh, huuh!?"
"I'm really sorry! After keeping you waiting this late for me."
"Why? Why? Didn't you promise to decide on our graduation trip with me today?"
"Tomorrow! I promise I'll do it tomorrow!"
"Is it really that important? More important than me? More important than being with me?"
"Today is the only day I can't. It's an important day… for my family."
"Ah…"
"…I'm sorry."
"Hey, Miyo-chan, try naming all the famous products from Hokkaido."
"Umm… Sea urchins, salmon roe…"
"Are you going to tell them you're in Hokkaido this time? You really should stop putting on airs for your daughter already."
"You're right. She should be honest and tell her daughter she's in the hospital and getting all the best care she can get. I'm sure that would put her more at ease."
"Don't talk about me like I'm not here, Miyo-chan. If something were to happen to me, you'll be the one who will have to learn to imitate my writing style."
"President…"
"If you end up dying, I'm afraid we couldn't keep it a secret for longer than a measly three years. All the newspapers will be writing about it, after all."
"Hm…"
"That's why you should listen to everything the doctor tells you so you can live much longer, President…"
"Ah… by the way, Nori-kun. Are you really free next month?"
"Indeed… if you absolutely insist on going, I'll follow you. I've even talked with the hospitals there, so you'll always be able to check in if something happens."
"…Right after I told her to live longer, she decides to come up with this nonsense."
"All the preparations are in order, but I agree with Miyo-chan… Are you sure you want to go to Vienna?"
"…This might be my last chance, after all."
"Why now? Why not wait until the weather is a bit warmer?"
"Could the letter you received last week have something to do with it?"
"You started bringing this up after you got that letter…"
"Miyo-chan."
"Y-Yes…"
"Being a mother means being responsible for your child, no matter what."
"If I need to be there for my child, then I should set everything else aside to do that."
"Youko-chan…"
"That's my god-given right as a mother, and I don't plan on letting anyone take it away from me."
"It looks like… Tomo is coming today."
"She said she'd 'come no matter what, so don't start without me.'"
"She's as selfish and inconsiderate as always… no one could guess from looking at her on TV."
"Well, no harm no foul. Let's wait for her. It's been a while since I saw her last, anyway."
"…When you put it that way, these gatherings have become kind of lonely. There were five of us back then."
"Nowadays, it's only you and me every time."
"Almost like a date, don't you think?"
"…What are you saying? Your girlfriend would be hurt if she heard that."
"You're the one who started it."
"B-But… is it really okay?"
"About what?"
"You have a girlfriend… yet you're meeting up with another woman every month like this…"
"Of course it's okay."
"But from her perspective…"
"If she gets angry about something like this, I don't want her as my girlfriend."
"Whether you're only going to stay as my friend or be degraded to a total stranger from now on, I can't think of a better friend than you in my life."
"…Takeya!"
"What are you getting mad for?"
"D-Don't try to use me as a replacement for Haruki! I… I…"
"I was just kidding, let it go."
"So what do you want to do until Tomo arrives? Wanna pass the time over some tea?"
"…Stop acting like just another girl."
"…Hey."
"Hmm?"
"Are, are you really…"
"Are you serious about your current girlfriend…?"
"Let it go. Not today."
"…You're right."
"Yeah, because today…"
"…Is a day meant only for Setsuna."
"…Huh?"
"What's the matter?"
"What's this link?"
After a long update on her condition filled with boasting and complaints, there was strangely enough a URL posted in the middle of the email.
"A phishing site? A virus, perhaps?"
"How suspicious can you possibly be of your own mother…?"
Looking at it closely, there's a compressed file format written in the URL.
In other words, it's a link to download a file stored on some server somewhere.
I click the link and save the file on my computer.
A few dozen files appear on my download bar.
"What is it?"
Under the link… and under numerous blank lines, Youko-san's message continued.
Yet the contents are about…
"It's been two years, so I thought it was about time."
The contents were completely different from the rest of the message, and were completely unlike her.
"This is about Ogiso Setsuna. About how she's doing after that time."
"Setsuna…?"
It's been two years.
It's the name that we've sealed away along with that country.
It's the name of the girl who ended up being hurt worst of all on the day when everyone ended up getting hurt, including ourselves…
The girl who I still couldn't bring myself to separate fromーthe girl who remains a part of me to this day.
The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth, the girl whose figure is still vivid in my mind two years later.
The download is finished.
But when I click to decompress the file, I start shaking from a premonition I don't understand myself.
"It's something you must accept eventually."
"Be prepared, and look."
Because the weight of Youko-san's words put Kazusa and me on edge.
"I'll open it."
"Okay…"
With my shaking right hand, I aim my cursor at the file, and double click it.
I grabbed Kazusa's hand, which was shivering just as much as mine on my shoulder.
Once the file was decompressed, I could see the file format. It was a video.
And in that video…
"Hey, Setsuna… don't frown like that, look into the camera and smile!"
"Don't tell me to do the impossible… I absolutely can't fail at this."
"So what if you make mistakes? We can just redo the video."
"That's not the problem. Today is the day I have to give my best performance…"
"I haven't seen Setsuna-chan this tense in ages. Must've been when she was rehearsing for the school festival last…"
"Don't say that, Takeya-kun!"
"Huh, what's that? Let me hear it, let me hear it!"
"Ah, I want to hear it too. Setsuna is always really calm on stage nowadays."
"Come to think of it, didn't you really hate Setsuna back then, Tomo?"
"Wha…"
"Right, right! She'd say things like, 'You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna' and wouldn't mind tricking anyone to put her down."
"Ooh, what's up with that? Let me hear it, let me hear it."
"…Takahiro-kun, you'll listen to anything as long as it's amusing for you."
"Wait, wait, everyone! Be quiet now."
"Oh, you're ready?"
"We've been waiting."
"Wait a second. I'll just adjust the camera… Alright, let's go!"
"Good luck, Setsuna… Show us the results of all your practice."
"While you're at it… show us your own self too."
"I will, thanks. Here goes…"
"Powder Snow."
("Are you doing well? I'm still singing.")
